source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon, 1999, Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
method: Additive source-specific transcription/paraphrase; genus-key traits labeled, historical rank concept cautions retained. No species gallery changes or BONAP.

morphology.habit: Small taprooted perennial behaving often as winter annual, milky latex
morphology.leaves: Basal rosette, usually deeply lobed along blade, terminal lobe often no larger than lateral lobes, triangular with straight or concave sides
morphology.heads: Solitary head per hollow scape, all yellow ligulate florets, outer phyllaries spreading/reflexed
morphology.fruit: Mature cypselae reddish/purplish or brownish-red; some inner phyllary tips may have a small abaxial knob in fresh specimens, difficult to see
morphology.pappus: Numerous white capillary bristles borne at tip of elongated beak
morphology.habitat: Lawns, urban disturbed areas, under trees

notes: 1999 source uses T. laevigatum, synonym T. erythrospermum; verify contemporary taxon limits before canonical transfer.
Source says introduced from Europe/west Asia.

records.original_name: Tetragonotheca texana Engelm. & A.Gray ex A.Gray

morphology.habit: Herbaceous perennial with stems 0.2–0.5(–0.7) m in original key
morphology.leaves: Opposite to connate-perfoliate, narrowly ovate, elliptic or oblong in overall outline, deeply pinnatifid, 3–10 cm long and to 4.5 cm wide (usually narrower)
morphology.heads: Radiate heads 2–4 cm wide including rays (genus), conspicuous four outer foliaceous phyllaries creating square-like bud
morphology.flowers: Yellow fertile pistillate ray florets and fertile yellow bisexual disk florets
morphology.fruits: Four-angled cypselae with scales or no pappus (genus)

notes: Distinguish T. ludoviciana by much broader, more clearly connate-perfoliate and toothed rather than pinnatifid leaves.

morphology.habit: Annual, leafy, branching stems to ca. 40(–60) cm; pilose to glabrate
morphology.leaves: Early rosette sometimes deciduous; cauline persistent narrowly linear 3–6(–8) cm long by 3–10 mm wide, foliage minutely resin-dotted (genus)
morphology.heads: Solitary long-peduncled yellow-rayed heads, phyllaries 2.5–4(–4.5) mm per key
morphology.rays: 6–22, ligules 5–10 mm according to historical key
morphology.fruits: Cypselae ~2 mm, awn-tipped pappus scales ~2 mm
morphology.phenology: Mar–May, secondary smaller heads to Jul

notes: Do not assign T. linearifolia var. linearifolia to a species-level photograph by default.

morphology.habit: Perennial 10–30+ cm with nearly basal leaves and mostly unbranched leafless scapes
morphology.leaves: Linear to linear-lanceolate basal blades 2–10 cm × 1.5–9(–11) mm, petioles 0.5–1.5 mm broad with clasping base, long hair in axils
morphology.heads: One yellow/orange-yellow radiate head on each leafless scape; phyllaries 4.5–6 mm per historical key
morphology.rays: 12–31 yellow rays, 8–22 mm ligules in key
morphology.phenology: Mar–May; occasional summer and Sep–Oct repeat

notes: Original flora covers species T. scaposa, not var. scaposa as a separate diagnostic entity; retain species measurements as source only and avoid claiming varietal confirmation.

morphology.habit: Annual or short-lived perennial, first-year flowering; 20–70 cm
morphology.leaves: Opposite and finely compound/dissected with many thin divisions, commonly spread up stem
morphology.heads: Radiate greenthread heads on naked stalks; outer phyllaries 3–12 mm and generally at least 1/2 inner length
morphology.rays: Ligules yellow to gold, sometimes red-brown at base, ~9–22 mm long × 9–17 mm wide with 3 apical lobes
morphology.disks: Yellow or dark reddish-brown corollas, lobes often long (genus)
morphology.fruits: Cypselae 3.5–6.5 mm; genus 2(–3) awns or absent, variable

notes: Historic flora recognizes var. filifolium and var. intermedium, and measurements must not be assumed for a particular variety without evidence.

records.original_name: Thelesperma ambiguum A.Gray [treated at species rank]

morphology.leaves: Typically concentrated near base/basal third (key); opposite, compound or deeply cut with narrow segments (genus)
morphology.heads: Solitary terminal head, ray florets yellow, usually present but occasionally absent
morphology.phyllaries: Outer phyllaries only about 1–2 mm, less than 1/4 inner length (key)
morphology.disks: Dark red-brown tubular florets with deeply divided lobes
morphology.fruit: Linear-oblong cypselae; genus pappus of small awns or reduced

notes: 1999 book treats T. ambiguum as species and puts T. megapotamicum var. ambiguum in brackets; current accepted rank and relationship require verification.
Do not substitute characteristics of rayless T. megapotamicum species description for this variety.

morphology.habit: Glabrous, frequently glaucous perennial 30–70 cm with few stem leaves
morphology.leaves: Opposite, upper third often 1–3 narrow segments, sparsely leafy
morphology.heads: Terminal golden/yellow radiate heads; inner phyllaries fused at basal 1/4–1/2 (genus)
morphology.disks: Yellow corollas with relatively shallow lobes, about 1/5 of limb length
morphology.fruit: Pappus absent or just two minute tooth-like awns

notes: Historic flora states T. curvicarpum is likely rare fruit form of T. simplicifolium or T. filifolium rather than separate species; do not create another inventory species.

morphology.leaves: Opposite, deeply divided into approximately 5–7 narrow linear lobes, scattered oil glands
morphology.heads: Solitary heads with peduncles 5–10 cm; involucres 4–6 mm high
morphology.phyllaries: Joined up to approximately half their length; free tips each have one or more narrow glands
morphology.fruit: Cypsela 2–3 mm, about 10 alternating awned/awnless pappus scales

notes: The opposite leaves and phyllary fusion/gland placement separate it from T. tenuiloba.

morphology.habit: Annual or short-lived aromatic perennial 10–30 cm, occasionally dense clumps
morphology.leaves: Mostly alternate and cut into 7–15 linear segments, gland-dotted
morphology.phyllaries: Fused almost to apex with short triangular exposed tips and an apical ring of oil glands
morphology.fruit: Cypsela 2–3.2 mm, pappus 10–12 scales 2–3.4 mm, each carrying 3–5 awns

notes: 1999 species treatment explicitly var. tenuiloba; var. wrightii has different leaves, do not propagate all dimensions to species without secondary check.

morphology.habit: Introduced Eurasian biennial with stout taproot, milky sap, 0.3–1 m
morphology.leaves: Alternate, clasping, grasslike narrow blades to 30 cm, long-tapering entire margins
morphology.heads: One head per swollen-tipped peduncle, opening in morning; typical ~13 phyllaries about 2.4–4 cm long
morphology.flowers: All ligulate lemon-yellow florets, no central disk florets
morphology.fruit: Cypselae 2–5 cm including long beak, pappus large plumose bristles, spherical seedheads

notes: Distinct from T. porrifolius purple corollas and ~8 phyllaries.

records.original_name: Verbesina encelioides (Cav.) Benth. & Hook.f. ex A.Gray

morphology.habit: Taprooted annual 0.1–0.9 m, stems NOT winged
morphology.leaves: Opposite lower, alternate above; triangular-ovate toothed grayish/canescent underneath; winged petioles often ear-like at base
morphology.heads: One to three showy terminal heads
morphology.rays: 10–15 yellow rays, ligules ca. 1–2.5 cm, tips prominently three-lobed

notes: Stems wingless unlike many perennial Verbesina; winged LEAF PETIOLE must not be confused with stem wings.

morphology.leaves: Mostly opposite, ovate-deltoid with cuneate base, harshly scabrous
morphology.heads: Few, often 1–10(–20); phyllaries broadly oblong/ovate with rounded tips
morphology.rays: 8–15+ spreading yellow rays 10–30 mm per genus key

notes: Regional key explicitly notes rare winglessness within otherwise mostly winged genus, so not a universal character for Verbesina.

morphology.leaves: Alternate, typically toothed, some extended down stem as wings
morphology.stems: Four- or five-winged, sometimes splitting with first freezing conditions and exuding water that forms ice ribbons
morphology.rays: One to five short WHITE rays, ligules to 10 mm
morphology.fruit: Flattened, sometimes winged cypselae, 2 awns or absent (genus)

notes: Freeze-triggered stem ice is a phenological trait, not reliable for identifying green-season plants.
